questions.text: What does Madina Tolenova study at WKU?
questions.hint: "I study Tourism and Hospitality at WKU — it is my second year." — Madina.

questions.text: The Zenkov Cathedral in Panfilov Park stands in the east of Almaty, near the mountains.
questions.hint: "Panfilov Park is in the heart of the city, between two wide avenues." — in the centre, NOT the east.

questions.text: Where is the Green Bazaar located in relation to the central post office?
questions.hint: "The Green Bazaar is about five minutes on foot from Panfilov Park, just BEHIND the central post office."

questions.text: Madina and Sabina took a ___ up to Shymbulak — a famous mountain resort twenty-five kilometres from the city.
questions.hint: "We took a cable car up to Shymbulak — a famous mountain resort high in the Zailiysky Alatau mountains."

questions.text: Why did Damir Yessimov get lost in Taraz?
opts: The woman gave him wrong directions
The street names on his map were different from the real signs
He turned right instead of left at the park
questions.correct: The street names on his map were different from the real signs
questions.hint: "The street names on the map were different from the signs on the walls of the buildings. It was confusing."

questions.text: A man in the park showed Damir the way to the Karakhan Mausoleum.
questions.hint: "A woman was standing at the gate of her house, watering flowers." — It was a woman at her gate, NOT a man in the park.

questions.text: The small museum on the ___ of the mausoleum had photographs and historical information about the building.
questions.hint: "On the LEFT of the mausoleum, there was a small museum with photographs and historical information."

questions.text: Which mausoleum did Damir plan to visit after the Karakhan Mausoleum?
questions.hint: "Later that afternoon, I found the Aisha Bibi Mausoleum — this time without getting lost."

questions.text: Where are the check-in desks located in the airport?
opts: On the second floor, next to the departure gates
On the ground floor, next to the café
On the ground floor, opposite the main entrance
questions.correct: On the ground floor, opposite the main entrance
questions.hint: "The check-in desks are on the ground floor, directly OPPOSITE the main entrance." — Aibek tells Kamila.

questions.text: The departure gates in the airport are on the ground floor.
questions.hint: "After security, go upstairs to the SECOND FLOOR. All the departure gates are there." — Aibek explains to Kamila.

questions.text: The shop between the café and the information ___ sells snacks and newspapers.
questions.hint: "One is between the café and the information DESK — it sells snacks and newspapers." — Aibek describes the airport shop.

questions.text: What does Marat tell Zara to do when she reaches the crossroads?
opts: Go straight on past the post office
questions.hint: "At the end of this road, you will reach a big crossroads. TURN LEFT at the crossroads." — Marat gives Zara directions.

questions.text: The tall red-brick library building is on the left side of the road after the crossroads.
questions.hint: "After you turn left, you will see a tall red-brick building on your RIGHT. That is the city library." — NOT on the left, but on the RIGHT.

questions.text: How long does it take on foot from where Zara is to the post office?
questions.hint: "About ten to twelve minutes. It is not far at all." — Marat tells Zara the walking time.

questions.text: WKU is located ___ Uralsk, which is ___ the west of Kazakhstan.
questions.hint: Cities and regions → IN. "WKU is IN Uralsk" · "Uralsk is IN the west of Kazakhstan." ✅ Not AT (for institutions, not cities).

questions.text: "The post office is opposite the park" means the post office and the park are next to each other, side by side.
questions.hint: OPPOSITE = directly FACING, across from. "The post office is opposite the park" means they face each other. NEXT TO = side by side — that is different!

questions.text: Damir walked ___ the park — there was a path that went from the entrance on one side to the exit on the other.
questions.hint: THROUGH = movement INSIDE a space, crossing from one side to another. "Walk THROUGH the park." ALONG = beside it; PAST = outside it without entering.

questions.text: Kamila walked ___ the departure hall and found her check-in desk.
questions.hint: INTO = movement entering an enclosed space. "She walked INTO the departure hall" = she entered it. Compare: "She is IN the hall" (already there, no movement).

questions.text: Walk ___ the post office — do not turn there — and carry on to the bridge.
questions.hint: PAST = to go by a place without stopping or entering. "Walk PAST the post office." ✅ Marat's exact directions to Zara!

questions.text: "The flight is in 10 o'clock" is a correct English sentence.
questions.hint: Exact times → AT, not IN! ✅ "The flight is AT 10 o'clock." IN = months, years, seasons. ON = days, dates. AT = clock times, specific moments.

questions.text: Madina visited Almaty ___ a long weekend ___ October.
questions.hint: Duration → FOR ("for a long weekend"). Month → IN ("in October"). "She stayed there FOR three days IN October." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence uses prepositions correctly?
opts: "The café is at the second floor, next to the security."
"The café is on the second floor, next to the security checkpoint."
"The café is in the second floor, opposite the security."
"The café is above the second floor, between security."
questions.correct: "The café is on the second floor, next to the security checkpoint."
questions.hint: Floors → ON ("on the second floor"). Adjacent places → NEXT TO ("next to the checkpoint"). ✅ AT/IN/ABOVE are wrong for floors.

questions.text: What does "breathtaking" mean?
opts: Very tiring and difficult to complete
Extremely impressive or beautiful, causing sudden excitement
Old and well-known but not very beautiful
questions.correct: Extremely impressive or beautiful, causing sudden excitement
questions.hint: "From the platform at Shymbulak, the view of Almaty was BREATHTAKING." = so beautiful it takes your breath away.

questions.text: A "stall" is a large department store with many floors and escalators.
questions.hint: A STALL = a small table or stand in a market where goods are sold. NOT a large store. "Sellers offered fresh fruit from their STALLS in the bazaar."

questions.text: Damir asked a woman at her gate for ___ — he was completely lost in the old streets of Taraz.
questions.hint: DIRECTIONS = instructions for getting somewhere. "Ask for DIRECTIONS." · "Damir asked the woman for DIRECTIONS to the mausoleum."

questions.text: What does "destination" mean?
opts: The place you are coming from
The route you use to travel
The place where someone is going
The amount of time a trip takes
questions.correct: The place where someone is going
questions.hint: "My DREAM DESTINATION is Istanbul." — the place you want to GO TO. From Latin "destinare" = to determine, to aim at.

questions.text: What is a "landmark"?
opts: A sign on a motorway showing speed limits
A well-known building or place that helps you know where you are
A map given to tourists at an information desk
A type of road that goes through a park
questions.correct: A well-known building or place that helps you know where you are
questions.hint: "The library is your LANDMARK — you can see it from most of the road." — Marat. A landmark helps you navigate.

questions.text: To "explore" a city means to stay in your hotel and look at a map.
questions.hint: EXPLORE = to travel THROUGH a place, moving around and discovering it. "Damir EXPLORED Taraz on foot." Active movement and discovery — not staying still!

questions.text: The Karakhan Mausoleum is over a thousand years old — it is a truly ___ building.
questions.hint: ANCIENT = belonging to a time long ago in history; very old. "An ANCIENT brick structure over a thousand years old." ✅

questions.text: What does "content" mean in "Damir came back tired but content"?
opts: Very energetic and excited after the trip
Quietly happy and satisfied with the experience
Confused and planning to try again
questions.correct: Quietly happy and satisfied with the experience
questions.hint: "Damir came back tired but CONTENT." — content = calm, quietly satisfied. Not excited (energetic) but peacefully happy.
